slides.0.title: Course Introduction
slides.0.content:
Anjou's rosé wines span an entire sweetness spectrum — from off-dry Rosé d'Anjou to the richly semi-sweet Cabernet d'Anjou. Meanwhile, Haut-Poitou, just beyond the administrative border of the Loire, contributes fresh, aromatic whites that round out this chapter of the Loire story.

AOCs Covered in This Lesson

Cabernet d'Anjou, Rosé d'Anjou, Rosé de Loire, Haut-Poitou
slides.1.title: Anjou Rosé Spectrum and Haut-Poitou
slides.1.content:
🌸 The Anjou Rosé Spectrum

Rosé de Loire: The driest of the Anjou rosés, made from Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon, Pineau d'Aunis and Gamay. Fresh, crisp, with red-fruit character. Minimum 3 g/L residual sugar — the Loire's closest rosé to Provence style.

Rosé d'Anjou: Made primarily from Grolleau (a local grape), with medium sweetness. Pale salmon color, light body, strawberry and candied-fruit notes. Hugely popular in France for casual drinking.

Cabernet d'Anjou: The most prestigious Anjou rosé — made from Cabernet Franc and/or Cabernet Sauvignon. Off-dry to medium-sweet (minimum 10 g/L). Deeper color, richer raspberry and spice, with pleasant acidity to balance the sweetness. Excellent pairing with spicy cuisine.

🏔️ Haut-Poitou

Located in Vienne (Nouvelle-Aquitaine, not in Pays de la Loire administratively), Haut-Poitou was elevated to AOC in 2011. Clay-limestone soils. The Sauvignon Blanc whites are aromatic and crisp; Gamay reds are light and fruity. An excellent value entry point to Loire-style wines.
slides.2.title: Quiz
slides.2.questions.0.question: Which of the following AOCs is covered in this lesson?
slides.2.questions.0.explanation: Cabernet d'Anjou is an important Loire Valley AOC and one of the core subjects of this lesson. It produces off-dry to medium-sweet rosé from Cabernet Franc and Cabernet Sauvignon.
